how: uv run python tools/mutants.py docs/quantities/qt-a3c/mutants-fix2.json --no-baseline --evidence docs/quantities/qt-a3c/evidence/mutants-fix2-run.json, after a passing build with the build pinned. A command that runs a test first rebuilds ve_service with the mutant and pins that build for the run only (lean/checkers.lock is copied back; a suite test runs with VE_LEAN_PREBUILT); a command that bypasses a proof edits the mutated file itself, whose exact bytes the harness restores.

mutants.claim: compiled code deduplicates the counted universals with the hash set (F5): without countedAmong's @[csimp] lemma it runs firstUse, and three times the request costs more than 4.5 times the CPU
command: set -u; cd lean && PATH=$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH lake build ve_service >/dev/null || exit 0; cd .. && T=$(mktemp) && cp lean/checkers.lock $T && PATH=$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH uv run python tools/regen_generated.py --write --only checker-pins >/dev/null; PATH=$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH uv run --frozen python -m pytest tools/bench/test_perf.py -k universal_dedup -q -p no:cacheprovider > $T.log 2>&1; cp $T lean/checkers.lock; tail -n 3 $T.log; grep -q 'FAILED tools/bench/test_perf.py::test_cardinality_universal_dedup_near_linear' $T.log && exit 1; exit 0

mutants.claim: the dedup's hash reads the whole statement (F5): a constant hash of formulas and bodies puts every statement in one bucket, so the hash set scans pairwise again
mutants.find:
deriving instance Hashable for VE.Time.QFormula
deriving instance Hashable for Body
mutants.replace:
instance : Hashable VE.Time.QFormula := ⟨fun _ => 0⟩
instance : Hashable Body := ⟨fun _ => 0⟩

mutants.claim: the hash-set dedup is firstUse (firstUseStep_inv, firstUseH_eq): a step that keeps an item without adding it to the set fails the proof
mutants.find: if acc.1.contains x then acc else (acc.1.insert x, acc.2.push x)
